title: Graceful overload absorption and dynamic token-bucket shaping for dedicated fleets
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Implement a combined rate-shaping and admission-control subsystem for Dedicated routing that provides throughput guarantees while enabling graceful overload absorption. The feature will use per-fleet and per-customer dynamic token-bucket shaping, latency-aware queueing with bounded wait windows, and a prioritized shedding policy. Goals: 1) Enforce committed throughput SLAs for reserved pools (steady-state guarantees), 2) Protect headroom for latency-sensitive traffic, 3) Avoid large-scale request drops by progressively throttling or downgrading requests during sustained pressure, and 4) Surface rich telemetry to Console for cost/latency breakdown and autoscaling signals.
design_notes: Token-bucket base: each tenant / route gets a refill rate derived from committed throughput and short-term burst allowance; refill is adaptive based on recent token consumption and queue trends.
Leaky queue: bounded priority queue per backend with a configurable max_wait_ms; requests exceeding max_wait are subject to soft-fail (fallback model) or hard-shed depending on priority and SLA.
Priority classes: latency-critical (P0), interactive (P1), background/batch (P2). Admission decisions consider class, token availability, and current tail-latency percentiles.
Predictive headroom: use short-window queuing metrics and model of inflight tokens to temporarily reduce refill for lower-priority classes to preserve latency for critical traffic.
Autoscaling hints: expose queue depth, token depletion rate, and sustained shed events as signals to Dedicated autoscaler; recommended policy thresholds included in PRD.
Fallback behavior: when shedding, route downgrades to smaller/quantized model variants if available; otherwise return explicit overload error with structured retry-after metadata.
Telemetry: emit per-request labels (route, tenant, priority, decision), metrics (tokens_granted, tokens_consumed, queue_wait_ms, shed_reason), and events for Console rollouts and incident analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Committed throughput tests: dedicated pool with synthetic workload should sustain configured throughput for 30m with p95 latency within SLA.
Overload scenario: when incoming QPS spikes to 3x capacity, the system should avoid simultaneous hard failures for >95% of latency-critical requests by shedding lower-priority work.
Autoscaler integration: queue-depth and shed-event metrics are available in Prometheus and used by the autoscaler to trigger scale-up in test harness.
Observability: Console dashboard shows token bucket utilization, per-priority queue lengths, and annotated shed events for the test window.
Safety: default rollout config must be conservative (low burst, short max_wait) and guarded behind feature flag + rollout policy.
Security review: KMS usage for per-tenant config and audit logging reviewed by security team.
progress_updates: 2025-02-12 - Created ticket and initial PRD sketch. Decided on token-bucket + bounded queue approach instead of only rate-queue to allow burst absorption.

2025-02-18 - Spike completed: prototype token-bucket library with pluggable refill strategies (static, adaptive). Found race conditions under high concurrency; added optimistic token reservation loop.
2025-02-24 - Design review with PM/Console teams. Agreed to emit structured shed events for Console ingestion and to include fallback-to-quantized-model as a first-class option.
2025-03-01 - Integration tests: simulated mixed-priority traffic. Observed ~12% tail latency increase when refill tuned too aggressively; adjusted predictive headroom parameters.
2025-03-04 - Security engaged for review of per-tenant settings storage; plan to use existing KMS-backed config store used by Dedicated control plane.
2025-03-05 - Implementation branch opened: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1427. Core admission loop implemented; working on telemetry labels and autoscaler hooks.
